question: Can an OpenZeppelin passkey smart account authorize the shielded pool's transact (deposit)?
method: In-process Soroban test (soroban-env-host 28.0.2) inside NethermindEth/stellar-private-payments@25f64658 e2e-tests, with the released Testnet proving/verification keys. No auth mocking for the transact call: the host runs the account's __check_auth, which calls the WebAuthn verifier on a P-256 assertion over the account's auth digest (preimage-v1).

artifacts.source: both fetched from Stellar Testnet on 2026-11-27
artifacts.token: real Stellar Asset Contract (register_stellar_asset_contract_v2), not a mock
artifacts.proof: real Groth16 deposit proof (policy_tx_2_2_AB) from the released Testnet proving key

authorizationTree.rule: default rule with one External(WebAuthn verifier, P-256 point || credential id) signer

implications: A client must sign the full tree (transact plus the nested SAC transfer) and two context rule ids.
The signature binds proof, ext_data (recipient, amounts, encrypted outputs) and sender, so a relayer cannot redirect it.
The relay policy for privacy calls must allow exactly this tree: pool.transact on a locked pool with one nested transfer on that pool's token, from the wallet, to the pool.
test: integrations/evidence/oz-passkey-pool-authorization.test.rs (runs inside the upstream e2e-tests crate; not compiled in this repo)
